{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjdzc8AAAABadkI2w", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IVzhED4R0", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IV", "number": 63, "title": "Schedule ordinary SH-2 MOV stores at their documented MA stage", "body": "## Problem

Related to #17

At `82ec9c509ac2e824a6de523c08e861d2978f8920`, `Cpu::execute` schedules ordinary loads through `LoadAccess` and separately schedules multiplier accesses. Ordinary MOV stores instead call the operand write path directly. Synchronous cache-array writes can therefore occur without an explicit store MA boundary, and ordinary stores have no corresponding MA/IF contention and successor-overlap model.

This matters when software publishes shared data, programs devices or hands work to DMA. Existing BSC buffering and device transactions distinguish acceptance from external publication, but do not supply the missing instruction-stage contract. Adding a uniform delay to every write would also be incorrect.

## Expected outcome

Implement the ordinary MOV memory-store pipeline on both SH-2s, integrated with the existing scheduler, replay journal, cache and bus transactions. Address/data preparation, MA qualification, internal acceptance and external publication must remain distinguishable. Preserve permitted successor overlap and existing write-buffer behavior.

The primary contract is the Hitachi [SH-1/SH-2 Programming Manual](https://antime.kapsi.fi/sega/files/h12p0.pdf), §§7.2–7.5 and §7.7.1, Figure 7.12, printed pp.185–186: ordinary stores have IF/ID/EX/MA stages and no WB stage. Cross-check the applicable SH-2 rules against the Renesas [Software Manual Rev.5.00](https://www.renesas.com/en/document/mah/sh-1sh-2sh-dsp-software-manual), §§7.1–7.2 and §7.4.1, Figure 7.21, printed p.438. Reconcile CPU stages with the [SH7604 Hardware Manual](https://github.com/luckyseoul/saturn-docs/blob/main/files/sh7604.pdf), §§7.3.1/7.11.2, before assigning buffered-write deadlines.

Scope covers every ordinary MOV store addressing form and supported byte/word/long width: indirect, predecrement, R0-indexed, register displacement and GBR displacement. Include their interaction with preceding loads, sequential fetch alignment and delay slots. Preserve existing system-register stores, multiplier timing, TAS locking, address-error semantics and device transaction contracts. Full speculative instruction fetching and unrelated instruction pipelines remain subsequent umbrella work.

Primary specifications and applicable corrections govern technical details. Agents may correct mistaken task assumptions with exact primary references and rationale in the source Issue, without human confirmation or weakening independent validation.

## Context and reproduction

Observed implementation:

- `src/cpu.rs:378–413` creates explicit load/multiplier phases; ordinary stores at lines 468–509 directly invoke writes.
- `src/cpu/timing.rs:305–340` implements ordinary load acquisition and successor overlap, with no ordinary-store counterpart.
- `src/bus.rs:1512–1527` permits synchronous cache-array writes and separately updates write-through cache state.
- `src/bus/transactions.rs` already journals scheduling decisions and retains buffered external writes independently of instruction replay.

Reproduce with an executing, warmed instruction-cache store kernel at both longword alignments. Record its write-request clock, local mutation or buffer-acceptance clock, external publication and successor execution. Compare against a separately authored manual-derived stage table, including synchronous and buffered destinations. Existing direct bus-adapter tests alone do not demonstrate the instruction pipeline.

Issue #55 supplied load-stage prerequisites; its validation explicitly leaves ordinary stores outstanding. Issue #51 supplied the SCU A-to-B startup interlock, which this change must preserve. The supplied snapshot lists no open task Issues and reports successful native, Wasm, browser and aggregate CI checks. Planning used read-only inspection; complete suites were not rerun.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Author a primary-referenced stage/deadline table before changing production scheduling. Cover 4n/4n+2 instruction alignment, one-clock and waited operands, successor overlap, preceding-load dependencies, and buffered versus synchronous destinations. Distinguish specification requirements from emulator phase conventions; do not derive expected clocks from implementation traces.
- [ ] Implement all ordinary MOV store forms on both CPUs. Independent CPU vectors assert effective address, retained source value, byte lanes, predecrement aliases, unchanged flags, once-only register updates and correct MA timing. Register-only MOV forms must remain outside this mechanism.
- [ ] Add executing native scheduler/bus vectors for cache RAM/arrays, write-through and cache-through RAM, representative on-chip MMIO and B-bus video writes. Check request, acceptance and publication before/at/after distinguishing boundaries, including write-buffer backpressure and a following external-read barrier. Preserve separately published B-bus halves and programmed waits.
- [ ] Verify shared-bus interactions using real peer CPU, on-chip DMAC and SCU requests. Assert retained payloads, peer progress, publication/IRQ ordering and the existing A-to-B startup qualification. Include a guest-visible data-publication handoff; hosts must not manufacture completion records.
- [ ] Cover pending-store replay, delay-slot completion, address-error dispatch, interrupt arrival, and reset before admission versus after acceptance. Preserve established manual-reset draining and power/system-reset cancellation. Native traces and results must agree across advancement chunks 1/3/17/10000, with and without passive inspection.
- [ ] Add or extend an original MIT-licensed SH-2 fixture executing on both CPUs in native Machine tests and production browser Wasm under `/saturn-rust/`. Assert independently predicted timing and arithmetic/readback records. Include changed-data, alignment/dependency and omitted-store controls, repeated cold boots, reproducible source/bytes/hashes, and a distinguishing negative control against the inherited implementation. Any retiming of existing guests must retain their substantive computation, device, pixel and audio assertions and document the independent derivation.
- [ ] Preserve Star Collector completion/restart, Prism Courier, Hardware Lab and existing load, multiplier, cache, write-buffer, reset, DMA, interrupt and video regressions. Pass `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo build --locked`, `cargo test --locked`, native all-target and Wasm Clippy with `-D warnings`, applicable CI fixture/media reproduction checks, `sh scripts/build-web.sh`, and the complete extended `npm run test:browser` without required skips.
- [ ] Update architecture, conformance and validation records with exact references, implementation/test links, actual results and remaining deviations. This completes only the scoped ordinary-store increment. Remaining CPU/peripheral, bus/reset/arbitration, SCU/DSP, video/audio, CD/media/HLE, SMPC and integrated #17 requirements remain mandatory. Hardware completion and genuine BIOS/commercial compatibility remain unverified; use plain references to #17 and do not reopen historical trackers.

## Optional validation

Additional deterministic store/dependency sequence coverage using an independently specified oracle. Personal firmware, commercial media, physical consoles, human approval and live Pages inspection are unnecessary.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
